==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|treten}}, from {{der|en|xno|treter}}, {{der|en|fro|tretier}}, {{m|fro|traiter}}, from {{der|en|la|tracto|tractāre|to pull", "to manage}}, from the past participle stem of {{m|la|traho|trahere|to draw", "to pull}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|trēt}}, {{IPA|en|/tɹiːt/|[t̠ʰɹiːt]|[t̠ʃʰɹiːt]}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-treat.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-treat.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːt|s=1}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|+|+|+,tret<l:Northern England,Bristol,colloquial>}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[negotiate]], [[discuss]] terms, [[bargain]] (''for'' or ''with''). {{defdate|from 13th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Tolkien Return of the King|passage=Now halting a few paces before the Captains of the West he looked them up and down and laughed. 'Is there any in this rout with authority to '''treat''' with me?' he asked.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[discourse]]; to handle a subject in writing or speaking; to conduct a discussion. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
#: {{syn|en|chat|discourse|parley|Thesaurus:converse}}
#: {{ux|en|Cicero's writing '''treats''' mainly of old age and personal duty.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=10|passage=Now of love they '''treat'''.|year=1873}}
#* {{RQ:Fielding Tom Jones| passage=And, indeed, should the excellent Mr Broughton be prevailed on to set fist to paper, and to complete the above-said rudiments, by delivering down the true principles of athletics, I question whether the world will have any cause to lament, that none of the great writers, either antient or modern, have ever '''treated''' about that noble and useful art.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To discourse on; to [[represent]] or deal with in a particular way, in writing or speaking. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
#: {{syn|en|bespeak|discuss|talk about|Thesaurus:discuss}}
#: {{ux|en|The article '''treated''' feminism as a quintessentially modern movement.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[entreat]] or [[beseech]] (someone). {{defdate|14th|17th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|Only let my family live, I '''treat''' thee.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To handle, deal with or behave towards in a specific way. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
#: {{syn|en|behandle|deal with|use}}
#: {{ux|en|You '''treated''' me like a fool.}}
#: {{ux|en|She was tempted to '''treat''' the whole affair as a joke.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To entertain with food or drink, especially at one's own expense; to show hospitality to; to pay for as celebration or reward. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''treated''' my son to some popcorn in the interval.}}
#: {{ux|en|I've done so well this month, I'll '''treat''' you all to dinner (or Dinner is my '''treat'''.)}}
#: {{ux|en|My husband '''treated''' me to a Paris holiday for our anniversary.}}
# {{lb|en|UK politics|law}} To commit the offence of providing food, drink, entertainment or provision to corruptly influence a voter.
# {{senseid|en|apply medical care}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To care for medicinally or surgically; to apply medical care to. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
#: {{syn|en|leech|make better}}
#: {{ux|en|They '''treated''' me for malaria.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To subject to a [[chemical]] or other action; to act upon with a specific scientific result in mind. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''treated''' the substance with sulphuric acid.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''treated''' the photo somewhat to make the colours more pronounced.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To provide (someone) with something special and pleasant.
#* {{quote-web|en|year=2012|title=Chelsea 6-0 Wolves|site=bbc.co.uk|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19632463
|passage=The Chelsea captain was a virtual spectator as he was '''treated''' to his side's biggest win for almost two years as Stamford Bridge serenaded him with chants of "there's only one England captain," some 48 hours after he announced his retirement from international football.}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# An [[entertainment]], [[outing]], [[food]], [[drink]], or other [[indulgence]] provided by someone for the [[enjoyment]] of others.
#: {{ux|en|I took the kids to the zoo for a '''treat'''.}}
# An unexpected gift, event etc., which provides great pleasure.
#: {{ux|en|It was such a '''treat''' to see her back [[in action]] on the London stage.}}
# A [[snack food]].
#: {{ux|en|These coconut and marshmallow '''treats''' are easy to make.}}
#: {{ux|en|Here are some healthy Halloween '''treats''' for ghouls and witches of all ages.}}
## A [[snack food]] item designed to be given to [[pet]]s.
##: {{ux|en|I lured the cat into her carrier by throwing a couple of '''treats''' in there.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[parley]] or discussion of terms; a [[negotiation]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} An [[entreaty]].
